newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ stowaway says planning to wed Malaysian crewman.
newsitem.headline: NZ stowaway says planning to wed Malaysian crewman.

text.p: A stowaway who said she and her twin sister jumped ship off shark-infested Australian waters plans to marry a Malaysian crewman she befriended during the ordeal, the New Zealand Woman's Weekly said on Monday.
The magazine, which often pays thousands of dollars for exclusives, said New Zealander Sarah Ingham had fallen in love with 29-year-old crewman, Ja'afar Bin Mohammed Zan.
"I'm in love with him. He wants to marry me," Ingham told the magazine. Ingham was hoping to travel as soon as possible to Malaysia to be reunited with her fiance.

Ingham and identical twin Joanne made headlines when they they were found at Coen, north of Cairns, Australia. They said they had jumped off the container ship Bunga Terasek with Ja'afar, floated for 20 hours and spent three weeks in hostile countryside before being rescued.
The claims drew widespread scepticism from Australian police and medical officials who said the trio's condition, when they were brought back to civilisation, was too good to be true.
But the twins said they did not care who believed their story.
"When we tell the truth no one believes us. It's like the the boy who cried wolf," Ingham said.
The twins were deported to New Zealand to face a variety of criminal charges and the crewman has returned to Malaysia.
The Woman's Weekly said the pair said they prayed a helicopter would find them as they drifted, tied together in lifejackets and lifebuoys taken when they jumped ship.
Australian authorities suggested the three may have been picked up by a passing prawn trawler and dropped ashore.
"We would have loved to have seen a prawn trawler," Sarah Ingham told the magazine.
"Just because we didn't get eaten by a shark or a crocodile...it's not our fault we made it," Joanne added.
